Japanese: 他の階は、良くも悪くもオフィスビルを思わせる近代的で清潔な内装であったが、その龍頭の居住となるその場所は、むしろ絢爛と言うべきだろう。白を基調とした壁面のあちこちに華美になりすぎぬ程度に金をあしらい、足元に敷き詰められた黒い大理石は鏡のように磨き込まれている。
old_english: For better or worse, the other floors had clean, modern interiors suggestive of an office building. The Longtou’s residence was better described as splendid. Gold adorned the predominantly white walls without tipping into excess, while the black marble underfoot had been polished to a mirror finish.
new_english: For better or worse, the other floors had clean, modern interiors suggestive of an office building. The Longtou’s residence was better described as resplendent. Gold adorned the predominantly white walls without tipping into excess, while the black marble underfoot had been polished to a mirror finish.
evidence: 絢爛 is more lustrous and ornate than generic splendid; resplendent is licensed by the gold, white walls, and mirror-polished marble.

Japanese: 暗闇通りと言うと、いくつもの風俗店を経営する壬生屋一族の名前がまず挙がるだろうが、この猥雑な通りではむしろ壬生屋グループの店舗はビジネスとしては非常に洗練された経営形態をとっており、多くはこの街娼やボロアパートに代表されるような原始的なやり方で性を売り買いしている。
old_english: The name most readily associated with Darkness Street was probably the Mibuya family, which operated numerous establishments in the sex trade. Amid the surrounding squalor, however, Mibuya Group businesses employed an exceptionally sophisticated model. Most sex on the street was bought and sold by primitive means—the streetwalkers and crumbling apartments being typical examples.
new_english: The name most readily associated with Darkness Street was probably the Mibuya family, which operated numerous establishments in the sex trade. Amid the street’s tawdry squalor, however, Mibuya Group businesses employed an exceptionally sophisticated model. Most sex on the street was bought and sold by primitive means—the streetwalkers and crumbling apartments being typical examples.
evidence: 猥雑 combines squalor with vulgar, gaudy disorder; tawdry restores that texture while the surrounding description supplies the squalor.

Japanese: 「……ノーマルの作る社会で落伍したタイプAを、何も知らないノーマルに逮捕させるわけにはいかない。せめて、同じタイプAである自分が逮捕してやろう。タイプAのことは、タイプAがけりを付ける。……これが、あんたが淡々と孤独な仕事をやり続ける理由です。切腹のときに武士が介錯してやるようなものですな。あんたは、そうやって悲しい義務感を背負って捜査をしているんだ」
old_english: “...You cannot allow a Type A cast out by a society created by Normals to be arrested by Normals who understand nothing. At the very least, you will arrest him yourself, as another Type A. Type As must settle the affairs of Type As. ...That is why you continue this lonely work so calmly. You are like a samurai serving as second at another man’s seppuku. You conduct investigations beneath the weight of that sorrowful sense of duty.”
new_english: “...You cannot allow a Type A cast out by a society created by Normals to be arrested by Normals who understand nothing. At the very least, you will arrest him yourself, as another Type A. Type As must settle the affairs of Type As. ...That is why you keep at this lonely work so dispassionately. You are like a samurai serving as second at another man’s seppuku. You conduct investigations beneath the weight of that sorrowful sense of duty.”
evidence: 淡々 is emotionally unshowy and dispassionate rather than serene; keep at preserves the habitual persistence of やり続ける.

Japanese: 灰上姉は強がってはいるがその顔は蒼白だった。殺人に慣れている、というわけでもないらしい。
old_english: The elder sister maintained a bold front, but her face was white. She did not appear accustomed to murder.
new_english: The elder sister maintained a bold front, but her face had gone ashen. She did not appear accustomed to murder.
evidence: 蒼白 is pallor caused by shock or fear; had gone ashen is the natural marked English image.

Japanese: ジェフリーは物憂げな顔で馬明にそう説明すると、
old_english: Jeffrey explained it to Ma Ming with a weary expression.
new_english: Jeffrey explained it to Ma Ming with a melancholy expression.
evidence: 物憂げ marks melancholy or pensiveness, not merely fatigue; the surrounding exchange supports the affect without resolving his inner state.

Japanese: この劉建志という人物のことはさほど嫌いではなかった。凶暴で頭は悪いけれど、その直情的でシンプルな人間性は、むしろ好きな方だ。子供の時からその豪快な行動の噂は聞いていた。
old_english: I had never especially disliked Ryu Kenshi. He was violent and stupid, but I rather enjoyed his direct and simple character. I had heard stories of his outrageous exploits since childhood.
new_english: I had never especially disliked Ryu Kenshi. He was violent and stupid, but I rather enjoyed his direct and simple character. I had heard stories of his larger-than-life exploits since childhood.
evidence: 豪快 praises bold, uninhibited scale; larger-than-life preserves that admiration where outrageous can imply offensiveness.

Japanese: 「まあ、あんなものは序の口だろうよ。今後、あいつはどんどん部下や街の連中の評判を落としてゆくことになる。無能の二代目と一緒にな。そこへ颯爽と、YSを救う新しいヒーローが登場するというわけさ」
old_english: “Well, that is only the beginning. From here, his reputation will continue to fall with his subordinates and the people of the city. The same goes for that incompetent successor. Then a new hero will make a dramatic entrance to save YS.”
new_english: “Well, that is only the beginning. From here, his reputation will continue to fall with his subordinates and the people of the city. The same goes for that incompetent successor. Then a dashing new hero will stride in to save YS.”
evidence: 颯爽と登場 combines dashing appearance with energetic entrance; dashing and stride in preserve both in the speaker’s self-aggrandizing register.

Japanese: ああ、私の、普段あんなことやこんなことをしている手が、こんな可憐な美少女の手を握っている！
old_english: Ah! My hand, the hand with which I habitually did this thing and that thing, was clasping the hand of this lovely girl!
new_english: Ah! This hand of mine—the hand I usually used to do this and that—was clasping the hand of such a delicate young beauty!
evidence: 可憐な美少女 combines delicate loveliness with explicit youthful beauty; the revised syntax remains exuberant while reading as intentional English.
哄笑 is loud, unrestrained laughter; roared is idiomatic and carries the marked force without embellishment.

Japanese: そう言って彼は眩しそうに笑った。
old_english: He gave me a dazzling smile.
new_english: He said it with a smile, as though dazzled.
evidence: 眩しそう describes how he appears while smiling, as though dazzled; the prior English reversed the image and made his smile dazzle the observer.

Japanese: 「蒼々たるメンバーだな。確かに、その連中を引き込むことが出来れば、ローズ・クラブに対抗出来る勢力になるだろう。……そしてそれらを率いるお前は、この街の王になるというわけか」
old_english: “That is quite a list. Certainly, if you succeeded in bringing those men aboard, you would have a force capable of opposing the Rose Club. ...And you, at their head, would become the king of this city.”
new_english: “That is quite a formidable roster. Certainly, if you succeeded in bringing those men aboard, you would have a force capable of opposing the Rose Club. ...And you, at their head, would become the king of this city.”
evidence: The source’s 蒼々たる is evidently the conventional 錚々たる sense: an impressive or formidable company; the revision preserves the emphasis without calling them illustrious.

Japanese: これは賢明な判断だったろう。この時期ＹＳはミス・ホワイトの尽力によって大量の武器を入手しており、のこのこ現れた木下組の面々を殺害し、そのあとの全面戦争まで見据えた計画を立てていたのだ。
old_english: In retrospect, that was probably a wise decision. With Miss White’s efforts, YS had acquired a vast quantity of weapons. The plan was to murder the Kinoshita-gumi delegation if its members obligingly appeared, then proceed into all-out war.
new_english: In retrospect, that was probably a wise decision. With Miss White’s efforts, YS had acquired a vast quantity of weapons. They planned to murder the Kinoshita-gumi delegation if its members obligingly appeared, with an eye toward the all-out war that would follow.
evidence: まで見据えた describes a plan made with the later war already in view; with an eye toward restores that forward scope without asserting that war was certain.

Japanese: 僕は目を開き、標的をまっすぐ見据える。
old_english: I opened my eyes and looked directly at my target.
new_english: I opened my eyes and fixed my gaze squarely on my target.
evidence: 見据える is a deliberate fixed gaze; squarely preserves まっすぐ without adding emotion.

Japanese: 今にして思えば、雑然とした裏路地を少し歩いたに過ぎません。特別に美しい自然を見に行ったわけでも、荘厳な建造物を見たわけでもないのです。商店に並んだ雑貨を見たり、空き地に咲いたタンポポに触ったりしただけです。テレビではもっと特別な景色を沢山みてきたし、なんなら部屋の窓から見える光景ともさほどかわりません。
old_english: Looking back now, we did no more than walk a short distance through cluttered back streets. We visited neither a place of exceptional natural beauty nor a magnificent structure. I merely looked at the sundries in shop windows and touched the dandelions growing in an empty lot. I had seen many more extraordinary sights upon television, and these hardly differed from what I could see through the window of my room.
new_english: Looking back now, we did no more than walk a short distance through cluttered back streets. We visited neither a place of exceptional natural beauty nor a majestic structure. I merely looked at the sundries in shop windows and touched the dandelions growing in an empty lot. I had seen many more extraordinary sights upon television, and these hardly differed from what I could see through the window of my room.
evidence: 荘厳 specifically evokes majesty or solemn grandeur; majestic is the direct natural contrast to the ordinary back streets.

Japanese: 私は銀色のAPTGを抜き、目の前で蒼白になる青年に狙いをつけた。しかし、失血のせいかふらふらとして、銃口が上手く定まらない。
old_english: I drew the silver APTG and aimed at the young man, whose face had gone white. Whether from the loss of blood or something else, I swayed too badly to hold the muzzle steady.
new_english: I drew the silver APTG and aimed at the young man, whose face had gone ashen. Whether from the loss of blood or something else, I swayed too badly to hold the muzzle steady.
evidence: 蒼白になる is a visible loss of color; gone ashen is more specific and idiomatic than gone white.

Japanese: さくらはまたふっと飛ぶと、向こうでこちらを不審げに見ているシウの側に着地し、顔にさっきまでの剽軽な笑顔を浮かべる。そして恥ずかしがって避けようとするシウに抱きつくと、そのまま二人で空に舞い上がった。
old_english: Sakura floated away again and landed beside Siu-kiu, who watched us suspiciously from a distance. The comical smile she had worn before returned. When Siu-kiu shyly tried to evade her, Sakura embraced her and carried them both up into the sky.
new_english: Sakura floated away again and landed beside Siu-kiu, who watched us suspiciously from a distance. The playful grin she had worn before returned. When Siu-kiu shyly tried to evade her, Sakura embraced her and carried them both up into the sky.
evidence: 剽軽 describes a playful or jocular expression; comical can instead suggest that her face looks ridiculous.

Japanese: 無理もないと言えば、そうなのかもしれない。正気をうしない、そして回復することのないと言われていた『発症』は筱喬にとってあまりにも絶望的で、これまでの彼女の人生全体を重苦しい悲劇の色調に染め上げていた。それがついに身に降りかかってしまったところで、あの人が颯爽と現れてその泥沼から引き上げてくれたのである。
old_english: Perhaps it was only natural. For Siu-kiu, ‘onset’—the loss of sanity from which she had been told there could be no recovery—was so utterly hopeless that it cast the whole of her life in the heavy colors of tragedy. When it finally descended upon her, that man appeared in all his glory and pulled her from the mire.
new_english: Perhaps it was only natural. For Siu-kiu, ‘onset’—the loss of sanity from which she had been told there could be no recovery—was so utterly hopeless that it cast the whole of her life in the heavy colors of tragedy. When it finally descended upon her, that man swept in and pulled her from the mire.
evidence: 颯爽 marks a brisk, dashing entrance rather than glory; swept in preserves the romanticized movement without inventing radiance.

Japanese: その間を我々は悠々と通り過ぎる。隊員たちは道の左右に立って苦い顔をしているYSの連中に嘲笑を浴びせる。YSの連中は顔を真っ赤にして歯を食いしばる。そんなに怒ったら、頭の血管が切れちゃうぜ。
old_english: We stroll leisurely between them. Our soldiers shower the grimacing men of YS on either side with ridicule. The YS men turn crimson and grind their teeth. Keep getting that angry and you’ll burst a blood vessel in your head.
new_english: We stroll leisurely between them. Our soldiers shower the grimacing men of YS on either side with jeers. The YS men turn crimson and grind their teeth. Keep getting that angry and you’ll burst a blood vessel in your head.
evidence: 嘲笑を浴びせる is concrete hostile mockery directed at people; jeers supplies the audible social action that abstract ridicule flattens.

Japanese: 彼らはトーマスのYSに敢然と反旗を翻し、YSと結びつきの強い店舗を襲撃したり、密告者として利益を得ていた人々を誅殺してまわった。滑走路通りでも何度も暴力事件を起こし、治安の悪化によって有名チェーンの店舗などは軒並み閉店し、残ったのは昔からこの町で商売をするものたちばかりだった。しかし、義勝はこの街を古くからの住人の手に取り戻すという目的があったから、それでよかったのだ。
old_english: They openly revolted against Thomas’s YS, attacking businesses with close YS ties and executing people who had profited as informants. They repeatedly caused violent incidents even on Runway Street. As public safety deteriorated, famous chain stores closed one after another until only merchants long established in the city remained. But Yisheng’s purpose was to return the city to its old residents, so this suited them perfectly.
new_english: They boldly rose against Thomas’s YS, attacking businesses with close YS ties and executing people who had profited as informants. They repeatedly caused violent incidents even on Runway Street. As public safety deteriorated, famous chain stores closed one after another until only merchants long established in the city remained. But Yisheng’s purpose was to return the city to its old residents, so this suited them perfectly.
evidence: 敢然と反旗を翻す marks a deliberate, bold uprising; boldly rose against is idiomatic historical prose and does not import moral approval.
